html:
The map's label, in its 700 snapshot, for the Cushitic-speaking peoples of the eastern Horn of Africa, in what are now Somalia, eastern Ethiopia and Djibouti. Despite the spelling, it is not the ancient Kingdom of Kush on the Nile, though both names go back to the biblical Cush.

These peoples were mostly herders of camels, cattle, sheep and goats on dry plains, the ancestors of the Somali, the Afar and their neighbours. Along the coast, small ports traded with Arabia across the Gulf of Aden, and in the centuries after 700 Islam spread from them inland.

The Christian kingdom of Aksum, by then in decline, held the highlands to the west. The map labels much the same area Cushites in 900.
